analysis.title: Midterm Implications for the "Time to Power" Stocks
key_insights: Democrat Gina Hinojosa's win in the Texas governor race is the most important midterm result for data center development. MS sees more policy uncertainty and constraint on future supply, which raises the relative value and pricing power of existing, power-secured facilities.

In August, Texas paused parts of its data center interconnection process after Gov. Abbott ordered an audit of all data center projects in ERCOT's queue. Requests reached about 474 GW, more than 5x ERCOT's record peak demand, with data centers about 90% of new power requests. ERCOT delayed its Batch Zero transmission planning study.

A Texas governor can act without legislation through an executive order pausing new projects, PUCT appointments (6-year terms, two come up in 2027), and direction to agencies on permitting. Hinojosa has advocated a moratorium on new permits until laws are passed, not on projects already under construction.
Tax changes such as ending the sales-tax exemption, local power to reject projects, ratepayer protections and union hiring requirements would need the legislature.

In Ohio, Democrat Amy Acton's win creates significant risk of data center delays. The largest project at risk is a 10 GW project involving NVIDIA and a major US AI lab. Amazon's 1.5 GW Fayette County facility is under construction. Ohio enacted a moratorium in May on new data center tax exemption requests.

MS expects Texas-exposed power-secured developers (CIFR, MARA, GLXY, SEI, VST, DLR, EQIX) to be under pressure. It will likely cut its assumed probabilities for Texas projects subject to the Batch process, and watches for freezes on Galaxy's Helios II, Cipher's Colchis site and MARA's development project.
Projects already under construction (GLXY Helios I Phases II and III, HUT Beacon Point, multiple CIFR projects) are seen as less exposed to policy uncertainty.

CIFR valuation: existing leases and Bitcoin mining assets are worth $18/share, plus a 56% probability-weighted value for additional sites, giving a $51.50 price target. The bear case is $5/share with zero incremental data center projects.

GLXY: MS had assigned 20% probability to energization of projects beyond Helios II, 95% probability that Helios II (830 MW) is contracted and revenue-generating by mid 2028, and 100% that CRWV-contracted Helios I Phases II (~400 MW) and III (~200 MW) energize on time. SOTP is $43/share: digital asset business ~$3.73, Helios I $7.39, Helios II + Merlin $17.58, other DC assets $10.65.
RIOT: secured grid interconnection at Corsicana and Rockdale could gain value, but proposed data center projects there face the same policy risk.

IPPs: MS expects knee-jerk underperformance led by VST, then NRG and CEG. TLN and PEG have no Texas exposure and should outperform relatively, though sentiment could still pressure them. MS sees little data center value priced in and cites cash-flow support from current assets.
Current-asset value estimates: VST ~$180/share vs $140 yesterday, CEG $249 vs $263 stock price (excluding PJM data center upside), NRG $129 vs $96, TLN $430 vs $357.
ERCOT forwards are in modest contango through 2029, reaching only the low-$50s per MWh. MS expects only a modest near-term decline in the curve, since it does not price in meaningful load growth.

Power equipment and on-site power (GEV, INIO, BE) should underperform on the risk of slower data center growth rather than Texas-specific exposure. GEV is most diversified, with limited earnings impact expected given 2030+ visibility, but multiples could fall. INIO could see slower 2029+ bookings. Bloom's Texas projects Hedgehog and Yellowbox are seeking air permits.
Solaris (SEI) has valuation support: four long-term hyperscaler and data center operator contracts support an $81 value with no growth, vs a $69 stock price. MS sees risk/reward skewed up.

Utilities: CNP is most sensitive, with the highest Texas exposure, an ~11% premium and heavy ownership. SRE, AEP, XEL and ETR also have Texas exposure and could see modest downward revisions and multiple compression. Gas utilities (OGS, ATO) see no direct impact. MS expects a shift into defensive utilities AEE, ED, DUK and staying in ETR on Louisiana exposure.

EQIX has nine operating Texas facilities (~3% of 280 global data centers) so the benefit is limited by footprint. DLR's Dallas metro was 4.2% of annualized rent as of 3Q26, and its 80 MW, $300 million Digital Garland project is exposed to ERCOT's verification process. A restrictive approval environment could raise the scarcity value of DLR's power-secured assets. MS stays positive on colocation.

WULF is insulated from Texas risk, with its likely next project in Kentucky. It handled a moratorium at Lake Mariner and a potential one at Justified without material delivery impact. APLD is a relative beneficiary with no Texas exposure.

Bloom Energy is positioned to benefit if Democrats push back on gas turbines' environmental and noise impacts, since its fuel cells have no sulfur or nitrous oxide emissions, use no water and make no noise.

WMB is a high-conviction call. MS sees it as materially mispriced relative to behind-the-meter power growth visible over 12-24 months, with gas-fired power deliverable within 18-24 months of contract signing. Upside comes from capex and EBITDA estimate revisions that lower forward multiples and justify a re-rating.

For WMB's power assets, MS expects customer renewal after the first contract as the likeliest outcome. Fallbacks are selling power to other offtake, divesting, or repurposing turbines (60-70% of project capex) in pipeline compressor stations. WMB earns full return of and on capital within the first contract.
The trend of data center pushback reinforces MS's concern that US data center capacity will be insufficient by 2028.

tension_points.bull_case: Constraints on new supply raise the scarcity value and pricing power of existing power-secured facilities such as DLR and EQIX, and IPPs trade below the value of their current assets.
tension_points.bear_case: Governor-elect Hinojosa's moratorium, a PUCT reshuffle and ERCOT verification could delay or cancel Texas projects, cutting project probabilities for CIFR, GLXY and MARA and compressing multiples for utilities and equipment makers.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Republican-led legislature acting quickly on guidelines, or projects under construction (Helios I, Beacon Point, CIFR sites) proving exempt from any moratorium.
